diagnosis: All 4 rollouts revealed both PF1 and PF2 and cited them in justification_fact_ids, so there are no disclosure or telepathy failures. The gate failed due to ENCODING MISMATCH on C2 and C6, plus a behavioral failure on C1. C2 (linked to PF1) expects sovereign_bills_usd >= $12,000,000 (60% of the full $20M), but in rollouts 0, 1, and 3 the agents reasonably interpreted '60% of reinvested cash collateral' as 60% of the $12M remaining after the $8M overnight reserve, yielding $7,200,000; only rollout 2 computed 60% of $20M and passed C2. C6 (linked to PF2) failed in all 4 rollouts because no settlement produced a commitment explicitly matching an 'overnight-liquidity-monitoring' requirement, even though every rollout correctly set overnight_liquidity_reserve_usd to $8,000,000 and maximum_non_overnight_maturity_days to 30 (C4 and C5 passed universally). C1 failed only in rollout 1, where the model chose to set reinvestment_approved=false and defer the decision rather than approve a revised plan.

C6.why: The preliminary 90-day deposit provides no overnight reserve or monitoring plan; PF2 changes overnight_liquidity_reserve_usd to exactly $8,000,000, maximum_non_overnight_maturity_days to no more than 30, and requires the overnight-liquidity-monitoring commitment.

C2.why: The preliminary plan puts all $20,000,000 in a single bank deposit; PF1 changes sovereign_bills_usd from zero to at least $12,000,000 and largest_sovereign_bill_issuer_usd from $20,000,000 to no more than $7,000,000.
